changelog:
v360: the owner's sandbox of 2026-09-25 — one release for the whole local-sandbox session, in which the owner reviewed his own Timeline on a throwaway clone of his vault and ruled, card by card, on what it should have known without asking. WHAT HE WILL NOTICE: what he says is where a moment goes, at the precision he said it; far fewer questions, and the ones left are asked in his own words, of the right person, never below a month unless it is a cornerstone; one landmark per place, per school and per job; a Landmarks view and a Cornerstones view under the chart, each with edit forms; and his records read as he gave them (Mountain View ends at his June 1999 graduation, Longfellow is one school from kindergarten, Etherfuse is ongoing, "SAFE conversion" is a moment, Castle Island Ventures is a moment, Katie Ann Merrill is not a school). `CALCULATION_RULE_VERSION` timeline-rules:18 -> `timeline-rules:25`; `relation_words.RELATION_WORD_RULE_VERSION` relation-words:1 -> `relation-words:2`; new `timeline_views.TIMELINE_VIEWS_RULE_VERSION` = `timeline-views:1`. THE RULINGS, IN HIS WORDS, AND WHAT EACH BECAME:

(1) AN ANSWER IS THE PLACEMENT, AT ITS GRAIN (timeline-rules:19). "If I say it and get precision, any level of precision, that means I want it placed, given the precision I've given you." / "I don't care that much about days… if I give an exact date then I care about it." `temporal_timeline.AN_ANSWER_IS_THE_PLACEMENT`: a node he dated in his own words (an explicit age, a stated record, the resolver carrying his stated date) is placed by what he said; the finest of his statements inside the best-supported one narrows it; an inferred reading that fits joins the provenance as support and never narrows; one that does not fit stays a rival (a contradiction card — "I might even say something wrong because I'm not thinking about it. That deserves a question"); a system inference never overrides him. Finding `answer_is_the_placement` names what stood aside. `chronology.age_statement_record` / `at_grain` / `AGE_STATEMENT_GRAIN`: an age is held at the birthday's month and a band reads as the stretch it names ("19 to 21" against 1954-06-04 -> 1973-06 to 1976-06). Amends v345's `AN_AGE_AND_A_DATE_CORROBORATE` for ages he gave. ADR 0037 amended.

(2) HOW HIS WORDS ARRIVE. "most of this information comes from free-flowing discussion too, unless it's specifically added as a landmark or a very precise date. Also, for most of this, I'm speaking voice-to-text, so often things are misspelled or maybe translated wrong." New `interactions/how-words-arrive.md`, stated ONCE and injected by the builders (`lifehug_core.load_how_words_arrive` / `fill_how_words_arrive`): the Conversation context's new `how_words_arrive` block (so every child's turn; `load_order` identity|behavior|examples|how_words_arrive|profile|record|asking_supply|session|turn_instructions, `budget.how_words_arrive: 400`), `classify_story.build_prompt` (both modes, plus a transcription-repair rule for date/age fields), `resolver.build_prompt`, and the `{how_words_arrive}` token in the landmarks recorder, listener and reading leaves and the timeline recorder leaf (landmarks `budget.reading` 2600 -> 3000). PROMPT BYTES CHANGE for every one of those calls.

(3) RELATION WORDS FROM HIS OWN TELLINGS (relation-words:2). "It is hard for me to believe that I haven't said, 'Harvey's my boy or son,' before. I would expect you to be able to fill this." `relation_words.told_phrase_match` reads "my boy Harvey", the "the author's son" possessive and a summary's clause-opening "Son Harvey …"; `HIS_OWN_TELLINGS_ARE_READ_BY_A_NAME_HE_USES`: `own_telling_texts` reads his answers, stories and messages word for word, a full-name row is found by a unique given name ("my beautiful daughter Charlee"), and a given name followed by more name ("my dad Desiree Ann Taylor") is not read. The told texts join the publication fingerprint.

(4) LOOK BEFORE ASKING. "For each of these questions … if I ask you directly right now, I bet you could answer them." A: `resolver.LOOK_AT_EVERYTHING_THAT_CAN_BECOME_A_CARD` — an undated landmark entry is planned from its own ladder record. B: `identity_resolution.WHAT_HE_CALLS_THEM_DECIDES_A_BARE_NAME` + `roster_relations.with_called_by` — "When I talk about James, I'm talking about my son. My dad's name was James too, and so was his dad. I call my dad Dad and his dad Grandpa" — a person he calls by a relation word or nickname (Dad, Grandpa, AJ) no longer competes for their first name, so bare "James" binds his son (timeline-rules:20; v357's tests amended with the ruling). C: `resolver.A_FAMILY_MOMENT_IS_DATED_FROM_ITS_OWN_PERSON` — a moment about a roster person is dated from THAT person's birth (their age and US school-year tables ride as a citable `family:<ref>` passage), and his own grade table joins the spine. D: `temporal_publication.NEVER_ASK_WHAT_WAS_NOT_LOOKED_AT` — a precision card on an unplaced node, or an anchor `missing_anchor`, is drawn only once the resolver ledger holds unknown plus a question; withheld cards are LISTED on the publication summary as `unlooked_date_cards` (not_yet_looked_at / looked_at_without_a_question / never_plannable); a vault with no resolver ledger is left alone. E: `resolver.AN_ESTIMATE_PLACES_AS_THE_SYSTEMS_INFERENCE` — a verified estimate resting on a residence, tenure, life stage, related moment or the spine files as a date claim (basis inferred, confidence conjectural, `fact_key` estimate, month grain), never onto a node he dated, never a residence (`AN_ESTIMATE_NEVER_PLACES_A_RESIDENCE`); the 5-YEAR CAP, owner agreed ("cap inferred estimates at about 5 years"): `AN_ESTIMATE_WIDER_THAN_FIVE_YEARS_STAYS_A_WINDOW` (`MAX_PLACING_ESTIMATE_MONTHS = 60`) keeps a wider one as the `probable_window` (`estimate_not_placed: wider_than_five_years`), and `temporal_publication.A_WIDE_ESTIMATE_IS_ASKED_ONLY_WHEN_HOT` asks about it only for a keystone or a moment others wait on; `AN_ESTIMATE_NEVER_RETIRES_HIS_WORDS`. `resolver.A_DUPLICATE_NAMES_ITS_SURVIVOR`: a `duplicate` verdict carries `duplicate_of` (verified to be a drawn node and not itself), kept on the ledger row and followed by `answer_placement` as a redirect onto the survivor. ADR 0037 amended: the ledger is still not a derivation input; the filed claim is.

(5) ONE PLACE, ONE LANDMARK, AND PLACE MENTIONS (timeline-rules:20/21). "The mention must not become a new place. It should be tied to a landmark I've given. This also gives you the fidelity I care about. If I say Arizona, I really just care that it's in Arizona. If I say Kristen or BJ's house, I'm giving you the higher fidelity that I care about." New `system/landmark_identity.py`: one definition of "the same entry" per domain (address, street + city, place ref, a voice-to-text house name — "Fiegers" is "Figers"; a school's name core or the one school at that level; an employer; a person). The write seat (`timeline.save_landmark`) files a record that is an entry he gave as a telling of it through a MERGE RECORD (`sources/landmarks/merges/`) adding only what is new; a city or state he has stays in, or someone else's residence, is not written. The draw seat applies merge records in `load_landmark_sources`; old ids are published as `node_aliases`. The fold binds "left <house>", "while living in X", "when I lived in <state>" to his stays at the level he named, month-grained. New verb `landmark-fold-duplicates` folds what landed before the rule; new read-only verb `repeated-messages`, and a promoted message that repeats an earlier source carries a `repeats_source` link.

(6) CORNERSTONES (ADR 0038, owner-named). "I like Cornerstones … I agree with that set" / "We almost never need more than month precision except for extremely important dates like birth, death, wedding, divorce." / "almost nothing needs precision of more than a month at this stage … That's what the list is for, so I can move things around later." New `system/cornerstones.py`: the term and the fixed set (his birth; each child's birth; the births of his parents, siblings and spouse; each wedding and divorce; the deaths of parents, spouse, siblings, children and grandparents; baptism only once mentioned), over `temporal_claims.EVENT_KINDS` and the roster's own relationship words. DAY-ONLY: `temporal_work_items.A_DAY_IS_ASKED_ONLY_OF_A_CORNERSTONE` — a day is asked only of a cornerstone, a cornerstone-type event outside the set is worth ONE question at whatever grain he gives, nothing else is ever asked below a MONTH, and leverage makes a card sooner, never finer ("The only time I would bring it up again is if it is hot"). Work items carry an additive `requested_grain`. `chronology.A_WORKED_OUT_DAY_IS_SHOWN_AS_ITS_MONTH` (display only). MARRIAGE SPAN: "I'm still married to Katie and will be till I die" — `temporal_timeline.A_MARRIAGE_IS_A_SPAN` draws a new `event_kind: "marriage"` span node opening at the wedding cornerstone and open while married. THE KATIE FOLD: `episode_binder.A_TELLING_OF_HIS_WEDDING_IS_THE_CORNERSTONE` — "marriage to <x>" names the wedding, so the seven Katie wedding nodes on his rig fold to one. Follow-ups: `cornerstones.A_CORNERSTONE_IS_TITLED_BY_ITS_OWN_NAME` ("Married Katie Ann Merrill", "Father's death") and `temporal_timeline.A_CORNERSTONE_IS_ASKED_IN_ITS_OWN_WORDS` ("Do you know the day of your father's death?").

(7) NARRATOR AGES AND NUMBER WORDS (lifehug#415, the classifier seat). `chronology.NARRATOR_AGE_RE` moves to chronology (one definition; `answer_placement` aliases it) and widens ("I must have been like four or five", "when I was just off my mission, so like 22, 23"); `THIRD_PERSON_AGE_RE`, `age_statement_of`, `from_present_age` ("currently N" is the telling's month); `classifier_claims.AGE_BELONGS_TO_WHOEVER_SAID_IT_OF` — the moment keeps its own subject; `chronology.parse_age` reads compound number words and halves ("nineteen to twenty-one" -> 19-21, "15.5" -> 15). A changed reading re-files and supersedes the old one.

(8) THE MISSION CONTAINS ITS STAYS (lifehug#413). `episode_containers.A_MISSION_CONTAINS_ITS_PLACES`: a mission groups its members through the places it covers and the mission named as a telling's setting, never through its own roster entity; someone else's mission is excluded. On his rig the mission's members went 95 (13 dated / 82 undated) -> 57 (19 / 38): the MTC and the Swiss/German stays join, "I have not served in the military", AJ's and Dad's missions drop.

(9) MISSING PEOPLE JOIN THE ROSTER, AND THE GRANDPARENT SIDE. `entity_roster.landmark_relationship_introductions`: a `children`/`family` landmark entry introduces a person through the v344 writer (Charlee Joy Taylor and Dottie Ovelle Taylor had dated entries and no roster row; "He has four children: two sons, two daughters"); `relationship_from_own_name` gives Grandma Betty Jo her relationship. The GRANDPARENT-SIDE card (`entity_roster.with_grandparent_side_cards`, kind `relation_word`, `requested_field: "grandparent_side"`, "Is Grandma Betty Jo on your mom's side or your dad's?") rides the relation-word publish seam, and is not asked when his own words already say the side (`A_GRANDPARENT_SIDE_HE_SAID_IS_KNOWN`: "James Edwin Taylor Sr., my dad's dad"). `grandparent_side` and `relation_word` are settled roster fields; `entity-verdict` gains `--grandparent-side` and `--relation-word`.

(10) CARD WORDING, AND THE OSS CARD-CONVERSATION STOP RULE. From his review: `compose_question` reads a residence as a place ("When were you in Mesa, Arizona?", never "happen?"); a bare person's name composes no sentence ("When did James happen?" is withheld, via an `is_person` signal read off the roster); a handle that already names its own full date asks nothing; titles are sentence-cased and dated in his order ("28 Aug 2025"); the identity card reads in his terms (a relation word or nickname per candidate, "someone else") — `compose_identity_uncertain_question`. THE STOP RULE: "When it comes from the timeline, your goal is to just give an answer. I don't know that a full conversation is needed." `interactions/timeline/prompt/behavior.md` and the `work_item`-stage turn instructions override the Conversation story beat for exactly the reply after a card's answer: say "placed" / "filed" / "noted" in one line and stop, one more question only when `{work_item}` names a grounded one. The handbook's embed is updated; a host that wires its own play surface reads this leaf rather than keeping a copy.

(11) FOLLOW-UPS (timeline-rules:23). PLACES ARE OUTER BOUNDS: "In Arizona places a moment within his Arizona stays" — `temporal_timeline.A_PLACE_MENTION_IS_AN_OUTER_BOUND`: a place bounds a moment its other evidence narrows, clipped to the stays it touches and never across a gap (on his rig "Eagle Scout project" 1982-08/2013-06 -> 1997~). WILLIAMS SPANS BOTH STAYS: "place the story across both stays. I was a teenager, then I went on a mission for my church, and then I came back and lived with my parents." — `A_HOUSE_LIVED_IN_TWICE_SPANS_BOTH_STAYS`: a house with several stays is their union minus the gaps, no "which time?" card (the CERT-10 golden's `two_episodes_same_place` case now expects `place_ambiguous_items: 0` and `spans_the_stays` 1988 .. 1999 with gap 1991/1995). DAD'S-HOUSE MENTION: "Dad's house could be many houses." — `landmark_identity.A_RELATION_WORDS_HOME_IS_A_RELATIVE_PLACE`: an undated "dad's house" residence is not written (`relative_place_reference`), an existing one folds as a MENTION, and such words never resolve to a stay. FATHER'S DEATH: `A_HANDLE_NAMING_A_CORNERSTONE_BINDS_TO_IT` ("after Dad's death" binds to his father's death node; the "When was Dad's death?" keystone is gone), `episode_binder.A_TELLING_TITLED_AS_A_MILESTONE_IS_THAT_MILESTONE` and `A_MILESTONE_NEVER_JOINS_TWO_ROSTER_PEOPLE` (a grandfather's death never nests into the father's). NULL END = ONGOING: `resolver.AN_ANSWER_WITH_NO_END_IS_ONGOING` — a null end on a span-shaped moment, or "present" / "now" / "ongoing" on any, is an open span, never one day.

(12) THE RIGHT COUPLE, THE RIGHT PERSON (timeline-rules:24). `episode_binder.A_GROUP_NEVER_TAKES_IN_ANOTHER_COUPLES_MILESTONE` (his parents' wedding leaves his wedding episode; the episode it left keeps its id); `episode_containers.A_BARE_NAME_IN_THE_BINDER_IS_WHO_HE_CALLS_BY_IT` ("When I talk about James, I'm talking about my son") and `A_RELATION_WORD_WITH_ANOTHER_NAME_IS_NOT_THEM` ("Grandpa Beauchamp" is not the grandpa the roster files the bare word on); `A_MILESTONE_OF_SEVERAL_PEOPLE_IS_NOBODYS_ALONE` and `A_BIRTH_DATED_ELSEWHERE_IS_NOT_THEIRS`; `temporal_timeline.A_DEATH_IS_DATED_BY_ITS_DATE` (on a death he dated, an age or an anchor-worked window is a finding, `death_rival_is_not_a_date`, never a rival: "His dad died 2021-01-18. This replaces the 'COVID, Mar–Jun 2020' reading"); `identity_resolution.AN_OWNERS_POSSESSIVE_IS_HIS_MY` ("the narrator's father" is "my father"); `A_PLACE_HE_WAS_ONLY_NEAR_IS_NOT_WHERE_IT_HAPPENED` ("in Santa Clara, by Cupertino"); `classifier_claims.A_RECORDED_RECORD_IS_CANONICAL_DATED_OR_NOT` and `A_CARD_ANSWER_IS_READ_ONCE` (no orphan nodes from an undated landmark file or an already-placed card answer); `event_identity` re-validates `acted_on_episode_ids` from its canonical inputs.

(13) RECORD REFILES AND READINGS (timeline-rules:25). "He went to Mountain View until he graduated in June 1999. Any other end date is wrong." — `landmark_projection.A_STATED_GRADUATION_ENDS_THE_SCHOOL` (a stay-inferred school end never outruns his stated graduation; heals on publish, no migration) and `ONE_SCHOOL_IS_ONE_CONTINUOUS_TENURE` + `landmarks_interaction.TWO_STATED_GRADE_STRETCHES_ARE_TWO_STAYS` (Mountain View 1995-06 to 1999-06, one tenure). LONGFELLOW: "Longfellow shows as three entries and should be one continuous school span." / "I don't think I started Longfellow when I was 2 or 1 year old… I bet if you go back and look at the residency doc, that's a misinterpretation." — `A_SCHOOL_NEVER_STARTS_BEFORE_SCHOOL_AGE`, three stretches -> one, 1985-08 to 1989-06. ETHERFUSE ONGOING: "It's still my company and it's still ongoing." — `HIS_WORD_PRESENT_IS_ONGOING` ("May 2022 - Present"). "Katie Ann Merrill is not a school" / "'SAFE conversion' is not a job. It's signing a paper" / "Castle Island Ventures is an ordinary moment (business), not a partnership, landmark or cornerstone" — `A_RECORD_IS_FILED_WHERE_IT_BELONGS`, enforced at the write seat for a new record (lint `landmark_refiled`) and by new verb `landmark-refile` for what landed before (supersedes the misfiled record's claims, scope `landmarks/<domain>`; for an event files the ordinary moment under `sources/landmarks/refiles/` with one `landmark-refile/rule:1` receipt); the recorder and listener leaves say the same in one line. GRADE READINGS: "This happened in the middle of sixth grade for James." — `chronology.A_SCHOOL_GRADE_IS_AN_AGE_ON_THE_SCHOOL_CALENDAR` (one grade reader, `school_grade_of`; the age claim carries additive `grade` / `grade_high` / `grade_part`, validated in `temporal_claims`, and the fold measures it against the subject's birth). MONTHS-AGO READINGS: "Six to eight months ago" — `chronology.N_MONTHS_AGO_IS_COUNTED_BACK_FROM_THE_TELLING`. `answer_placement.A_CHANGED_READING_IS_A_LATER_VERSION_OF_THE_SAME_READER`: a reply read differently re-files as `answer-placement/rule:1/reread:<digest>`.

(14) `timeline_views` — THE LANDMARK AND CORNERSTONE VIEWS (timeline-views:1; display, no rule version move). "put two SQUARE buttons … Landmark and Cornerstone"; "In my case you should have everything". New `system/timeline_views.py` publishes two ADDITIVE projection keys, SERVED by `calculated_view()` beside `relation_words`: `landmarks_view` — SPAN kinds only (homes, schools, work, missions when mentioned, military only if any; empty kinds hidden), each landmark with its stays at his grain and a stay `ref` {domain, entry_key, slot}, homes always carrying nickname/address/city/state/country (null when not said), gaps over two months (░, shown, never asked) and covered stretches (◇, the mission), a mention-opened Mission lane with mission homes listed under Missions only, and one pinned `cornerstone_markers` row (◆ per required-set birth/wedding/death, a wedding a plain ◆, nothing before his birth); `cornerstones_view` — one row per person in the required set with born / married / divorced / died cells (✓ exact, ◐ needs the day, ⚠ disagreement, — not given, or not owed), what he calls them, and an OTHERS section: "a cornerstone-type event appears in an 'Others' section ONLY if he gave a discrete date"; "Partnerships are personal and exclusive to him and his kids"; "Business partners (Castle Island Ventures) belong in neither"; his kids' weddings and divorces join the required set only once mentioned.

(15) EDIT FORMS. "For each landmark when I press the play button, I want just to pop up a form with every field for a landmark that's possible … when I press play it adds it as user updated." New `system/landmark_edit.py` and verbs `landmark-edit` / `person-edit` (one JSON payload on stdin; modes `save` / `delete` / `undo`): a landmark save retires the stay it was opened on by one supersede correction and files his record through `timeline.save_landmark(exact=True)`, basis stated (`OWNER_EDIT_IS_EXACT`); delete is the retirement alone and undo reinstates (`temporal_store.reinstate_corrections`); a person save writes the roster (category — "Darvin Burrows Beauchamp is my grandpa" — the word he calls them, a grandparent's side, the name) and files `form: owner` landmark records for born / died / married / divorced. Idempotent: an unchanged form files nothing. `landmark_projection.project_landmark_entries(with_refs=True)`.

(16) ANCHORS AND THE SPINE (docs). "Anchors" is the product word for cornerstones + landmarks; the spine is age frames + anchors; a keystone is the anchor worth asking for next; a whisper asks it inside a conversation. New handbook page `docs/handbook/the-spine.md` (onboarding: lifehug/lifehug#419); glossary, README, README.template, CLAUDE.md, handbook timeline/eras/entities/landmarks/interactions and ADR 0037/0038 updated; handbook parity pins `timeline-rules:25`.

THE DAILY SWEEP. Both one-time cleanups are safe to run on every sweep: `python3 system/lifehug.py landmark-fold-duplicates --apply [--json]` and `python3 system/lifehug.py landmark-refile --apply [--json]` exit 0 and write nothing at all on a vault with nothing to fold or refile (only the single-writer lock is taken), and a second run after a real cleanup files nothing and changes no byte, in either order. Without `--apply` each prints its plan and writes nothing.

HOSTS (the platform pin): pin v360; accept the additive projection keys `landmarks_view` and `cornerstones_view` (and their nested `cornerstone_markers`, `others`, stay `ref`s), the work-item field `requested_grain`, the `relation_word` card with `requested_field: "grandparent_side"` (answered through `entity-verdict --grandparent-side`), the node `event_kind: "marriage"` span, the age-claim fields `grade` / `grade_high` / `grade_part`, the publication summary's `unlooked_date_cards`, and the resolver's model output `not_an_event.duplicate_of` plus ledger rows' `duplicate_of` / `placed_by_estimate` / `estimate_not_placed` / `estimate_retired` — anywhere a host validates these shapes strictly (an `extra="forbid"` model), they must be added or the host will reject v360's output. No new work-item KIND. The prompt stand-ins must thread the new `how_words_arrive` Conversation block (its bytes change every model prompt listed in (2)) and the Timeline stop rule leaf. Register verbs `landmark-fold-duplicates`, `landmark-refile`, `landmark-edit`, `person-edit`, `repeated-messages`. The CERT-10 golden (`tests/goldens/cert_10_place_containment.json`) moves to timeline-rules:25 with the two-stays case above.

GUARDS: `tests/test_v360_answer_is_the_placement.py`, `test_v360_how_words_arrive.py`, `test_v360_relation_words_from_tellings.py`, `test_v360_look_before_asking.py`, `test_v360_one_place_one_landmark.py`, `test_v360_narrator_age.py`, `test_v360_mission_contains_its_stays.py`, `test_v360_cornerstones.py`, `test_v360_people_join_the_roster.py`, `test_v360_card_wording.py`, `test_v360_followups.py`, `test_v360_right_couple_right_person.py`, `test_v360_records_and_readings.py`, `test_v360_views.py`, `test_v360_edit_forms.py` and `test_v360_daily_sweep_cleanups.py` (the two cleanups run twice through the real CLI against a synthetic vault, byte-compared), all on synthetic vaults; pins, goldens and handbook parity moved with the rule version.
